blocks.h2: Water Treatment Options for Algonquin Homes

tiles.body: Reduce the minerals that cause scale, spots and sediment in the water heater.
Reduce chlorine taste and odor and catch sediment.
Under-sink reverse osmosis for cooking and drinking.
Settings, salt, resin and valve repairs on the softener you already have.

bodies: Algonquin's water comes from nine village wells, most of them shallow and one about 1,300 feet deep, treated at three plants on both sides of the Fox River. Groundwater carries minerals, and the village's own report lists water softener regeneration as one source of sodium in the system, as one source of sodium in the system.

A test at your tap shows hardness and other things that affect taste, scale and appliances. It also tells you whether your softener is actually doing its job. We use the results to recommend only what your home needs.

blocks.intro: Water testing draws steady search interest in Algonquin.

items.body: Groundwater picks up minerals from the rock it moves through. That shows up as scale on fixtures and sediment in the water heater.

items.h3: Softeners Are Common, and So Are Tired Ones
items.body: Many softeners were installed with the house in the 1990s and 2000s. Worn resin or wrong settings let hardness right through.
A carbon filter improves taste and smell at the kitchen tap or the whole house.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.preview: Groundwater naturally carries minerals. A test shows your exact hardness.
items.answer: Algonquin's water comes from village wells, and groundwater naturally carries minerals. A test at your tap tells you exactly how hard yours is, so you can decide on a softener with real numbers.

items.q: How do I know if my softener is working?
items.preview: Test the water. Spots and scale are clues.
items.answer: Test the water after the softener. White spots, scale on fixtures and soap that won't lather are signs it isn't keeping up.

items.q: Can you repair my existing softener?
items.answer: Often, yes. Settings, valves and resin can be serviced or replaced. If it's beyond repair, we'll tell you.

items.q: How often should filters be changed?
items.preview: Most cartridges every few months to a year.
items.answer: It depends on the system and your use. Most cartridges last a few months to a year.

items.q: What does a water softener or filter cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the system. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the type and size of the system and how it connects. We quote a flat rate before we start.
